When it comes to the IELTS Speaking section, many aspirants step back to attempt this. But the great thing you must understand is, there is nothing to fear if you are indulged in proper preparation of IELTS Speaking. Following the below mentioned strategies will be a key to success. This will definitely help you in attempting this section without any kind of fear. IELTS Speaking test has three parts – Introduction, Cue Card and Discussion Round. Here everything happens on the spur of the moment, so you must be spontaneous. The IELTS Speaking preparation is important as your first response needs to be your best effort.

Proven Tips for IELTS Speaking Preparation

  • You must be Aware of the Timing and Scoring in IELTS Speaking – In the introduction part, it generally lasts for 4-5 minutes. Here you must consider being relevant and speak only about the question asked, give answers but do not talk for too long and you can use this part to develop your fluency and confidence. The send part will be speaking on the cue card. Here the tips you can follow are making useful notes that will help you speak for a long time, refer to the cue card to design the structure of your talk and you must make sure your speech is long enough for 2-3 minutes. The third part will be the discussion round. Here you must know relevant information about the topic, support and extend your answers to make it look confident and you can re-phrase the question to understand what the examiner is expecting.
  • Don’t try Speaking Prepared Answers – Many of the IELTS aspirants try to memorize the answers as many as in the school or colleges. But it will not help you as there are possibilities to have an unaware or random topic in the cue card. The Casper Academy of Excellence is giving best guidance with one-to-one coaching and is the best IELTS coaching centre in Kerala.
  • Fluency vs. Vocabulary – Many of the IELTS aspirants is getting confused in maintaining consistency between fluency and vocabulary. You must understand that these skills carry same weightage. It is advisable to be fluent during the exam rather than thinking of best word to use.
  • Be Natural When you Speak – Avoid speaking in monotone. You must speak naturally to engage the listener. You can also vary your pitch at several points to sound more fluent and interesting.
  • Don’t Panic When you Make Mistakes – It is fine when you make mistakes while speaking. Mistakes may occur when you talk quickly or uttering a word accidentally. Don’t panic in such situations.
